This is an ownership role for an individual who can independently design, implement, troubleshoot, and operate production systems without day‑to‑day guidance from another AWS specialist.

Key Responsibilities

AWS Infrastructure & Linux Operations - Design, configure, and operate AWS environments using services such as ECS, ECR, EC2, VPC, ALB/NLB, Route 53, ACM, IAM, RDS, ElastiCache, Amazon MQ, and S3. - Administer Ubuntu/Linux systems, Nginx reverse proxies, TLS certificates, DNS, networking, system services, permissions, storage, and resource utilisation. - Design secure network boundaries, service‑to‑service connectivity, environment separation, and production access patterns. - Troubleshoot production incidents independently and document architecture, operational procedures, and recovery steps.

Infrastructure as Code & CI/CD - Build and maintain infrastructure using Terraform and/or AWS CloudFormation; keep it reproducible, reviewed, and version‑controlled. - Develop and maintain GitHub Actions and/or Bitbucket Pipelines for builds, tests, container publishing, deployment, and release approvals. - Implement safe release strategies, health checks, database migration practices, rollback procedures, and deployment traceability. - Automate routine infrastructure and operational tasks using shell scripting and, where useful, Python.

  • Hands‑on experience with ECS, ECR, IAM, VPC, load balancers, CloudWatch, and managed data services.
  • Production CI/CD experience with GitHub Actions and/or Bitbucket Pipelines.
  • Practical IaC experience with Terraform or CloudFormation.

Responsibilities

  • Own the growth plan and its implementation. Set quarterly targets across acquisition, onboarding, engagement and retention, sequence the work, and be accountable for shipping it.
  • Own the numbers end‑to‑end: sign‑ups, activation rate, free‑to‑paid conversion, cohort retention, churn, expansion revenue and CAC payback.
  • Acquisition: lead organic, paid, product‑led, AI search and marketplace channels; decide quarterly budget and effort allocation.
  • Onboarding: own the path from install to a live consent banner; work with product to cut steps, reduce drop‑off, and deliver first value quickly.
  • Engagement: build lifecycle programmes across email, in‑app messaging and in‑product prompts to bring users back and deepen usage.
  • Retention & churn: track cohort retention, diagnose attrition, run win‑back/reactivation, and implement structural fixes.
  • Expansion: drive upgrades, design usage‑based triggers, and test pricing/packaging with product and finance.
  • Build and run the experimentation roadmap across website, onboarding, pricing page, in‑app upgrade paths and lifecycle email.
  • Build the growth reporting layer: define key metrics, instrument them, and make numbers legible to the wider team.
  • Partner with Global Partnerships and Affiliate teams to align channel growth.
  • Manage and mentor a small team of specialists (performance, lifecycle, SEO, AI search) and hire to fill gaps.

  • Run a weekly growth review: what was shipped, what moved, what we are killing.

  • You will own the number, not just contribute; if growth lags, you decide and act early.
  • Experiment velocity is a standing expectation – prefer ten tests with six losers over two slow tests.
  • No backlog handed to you; you must identify constraints, decide actions, and start.

  • Small team, no layers, direct access to leadership and product; no permission‑seeking required.
